verdict.label: HOLD — Morning Call Confirmed; SPX 14 Points Shy of BUY; Bogus Iran Rally Masks Unresolved Regime
verdict.rationale_short: The morning's core prediction executed with precision: NVDA's beats-and-drops closed at $219.45 (called from $226 AH; -2.93% historical pattern matched exactly), and SPX closed at 7,445.72 — 14 points below the 7,460 BUY trigger for the fourth consecutive session. The day was rescued from a down close only by a late-session bogus report that the US and Iran were near a draft resolution, sending oil briefly below $100 before reversing to ~$101. The Dow hit a record 50,285 (no NVDA exposure), but the macro regime — 30Y at 5.10%, VIX at 17.44, SPX below the trigger — is not cleared. NVDA is now in the $216–220 target entry zone; Friday is Day 2 of the consolidation test. Hold through pre-Memorial Day light volume; April PCE on May 28 is the macro binary.

bear_case: The Dow's record close at 50,285 and VIX declining to 17.44 are genuine improvements in market breadth and risk appetite — if these represent institutional rotation into cyclicals rather than a fake-news-driven spike, the SPX re-rate through 7,460 follows on Friday's thin-volume drift and the HOLD call is one session too conservative. NVDA's $219.45 close rather than a collapse toward $210 is a constructive digestion, and the $80B buyback authorization provides a structural put. A Friday close above 7,460 with 30Y at or below 5.05% would arm the BUY immediately for Tuesday's post-holiday open. If SPX closes above 7,460 on Friday and 30Y closes at or below 5.05%, the HOLD call is wrong — upgrade to BUY before markets close.
